texts.value: Promotes two parallel branches of the DNA damage tolerance (DDT) pathway (also known as the post-replication repair (PRR) pathway) that bypass replication-blocking lesions without removing them; the translesion DNA synthesis (TLS) branch and the template-switching (TS) branch (PubMed:10880451, PubMed:10924462, PubMed:11884624, PubMed:12226657, PubMed:12496280, PubMed:1324406, PubMed:17936713, PubMed:23142547, PubMed:25690888, PubMed:27001510, PubMed:29742437, PubMed:31350889, PubMed:33436623, PubMed:36623584, PubMed:37594077, PubMed:7961763, PubMed:9016623). To facilitate translesion DNA synthesis, recruits deoxycytidyl transferase/scaffolding protein REV1 to monoubiquitinated POL30/PCNA; this is required for translesion synthesis at 1,N6-ethenoadenine DNA adducts (PubMed:23142547, PubMed:27001510, PubMed:37594077). To initiate template-switching, catalyzes the 'Lys-63'-linked polyubiquitination of monoubiquitinated POL30/PCNA, in conjunction with the ubiquitin-conjugating enzymes MMS2 and UBC13 (PubMed:10880451, PubMed:11884624, PubMed:12226657, PubMed:12496280). In the chicken foot model of template switching, drives the ATP-dependent unwinding of the leading arm, which results in replication fork reversal and formation of a four-way DNA junction termed a chicken foot intermediate (PubMed:1324406, PubMed:17936713, PubMed:25690888, PubMed:29742437, PubMed:31350889, PubMed:33436623, PubMed:36623584, PubMed:7961763). In the chicken foot intermediate, the template is switched from the stalled leading strand to the newly synthesized sister/lagging strand, that can be extended by DNA polymerases; this results in the bypass of the DNA damage in the leading strand once the extended chicken foot is converted back to a replication fork (PubMed:1324406, PubMed:17936713, PubMed:25690888, PubMed:29742437, PubMed:31350889, PubMed:33436623, PubMed:36623584, PubMed:7961763). The enzyme reportedly lacks classical helicase activity; its ATPase activity is dependent upon binding of replication fork-like DNA, and it has been shown to catalyze the concerted unwinding and annealing of nascent and parental strands without exposing extended single-stranded regions, or to only unwind the leading arm (PubMed:17936713, PubMed:25690888, PubMed:7961763). Has also been implicated in double-strand break repair, possibly by circumventing non-homologous end-joining (PubMed:16224103, PubMed:9016623)

texts.value: Catalyzes the last step in the trans-sulfuration pathway from L-methionine to L-cysteine in a pyridoxal-5'-phosphate (PLP)-dependent manner, which consists on cleaving the L,L-cystathionine molecule into L-cysteine, ammonia and 2-oxobutanoate (PubMed:10212249, PubMed:18476726, PubMed:19261609, PubMed:19961860). Part of the L-cysteine derived from the trans-sulfuration pathway is utilized for biosynthesis of the ubiquitous antioxidant glutathione (PubMed:18476726). Besides its role in the conversion of L-cystathionine into L-cysteine, it utilizes L-cysteine and L-homocysteine as substrates (at much lower rates than L,L-cystathionine) to produce the endogenous gaseous signaling molecule hydrogen sulfide (H2S) (PubMed:10212249, PubMed:19019829, PubMed:19261609, PubMed:19961860). In vitro, it converts two L-cysteine molecules into lanthionine and H2S, also two L-homocysteine molecules to homolanthionine and H2S, which can be particularly relevant under conditions of severe hyperhomocysteinemia (which is a risk factor for cardiovascular disease, diabetes, and Alzheimer's disease) (PubMed:19261609). Lanthionine and homolanthionine are structural homologs of L,L-cystathionine that differ by the absence or presence of an extra methylene group, respectively (PubMed:19261609). Acts as a cysteine-protein sulfhydrase by mediating sulfhydration of target proteins: sulfhydration consists of converting -SH groups into -SSH on specific cysteine residues of target proteins such as GAPDH, PTPN1 and NF-kappa-B subunit RELA, thereby regulating their function (PubMed:22169477). By generating the gasotransmitter H2S, it participates in a number of physiological processes such as vasodilation, bone protection, and inflammation (Probable) (PubMed:29254196). Plays an essential role in myogenesis by contributing to the biogenesis of H2S in skeletal muscle tissue (By similarity). Can also accept homoserine as substrate (By similarity). Catalyzes the elimination of selenocystathionine (which can be derived from the diet) to yield selenocysteine, ammonia and 2-oxobutanoate (By similarity)

texts.value: ATP-dependent transporter of the ATP-binding cassette (ABC) family that hydrolyzes ATP to enable the active transport of organic anions conjugated with glutathione, glucuronate or sulfate. Operates at the plasma membrane where it mediates the efflux of substrates from the cytoplasm into the extracellular space. The rate of transport is in some way coupled to the reduced glutathione (GSH) intracellular levels (PubMed:10064732, PubMed:11114332, PubMed:16230346, PubMed:8640791, PubMed:7961706, PubMed:9281595). Mediates the systemic release of glutathione-conjugated leukotriene C4 (LTC4) from myeloid cells such as mast cells, as part of the inflammatory response (PubMed:10064732, PubMed:11114332, PubMed:7961706, PubMed:8640791). Exports S-geranylgeranyl-glutathione (GGG) in lymphoid cells and stromal compartments of lymphoid organs. ABCC1 (via extracellular transport) with GGT5 (via GGG catabolism) establish GGG gradients within lymphoid tissues to position P2RY8-positive lymphocytes at germinal centers in lymphoid follicles and restrict their chemotactic transmigration from blood vessels to the bone marrow parenchyma (By similarity). Mediates basolateral export of GSH-conjugated R- and S-prostaglandin A2 diastereomers in polarized epithelial cells (PubMed:9426231). Can export both GSH and its oxidized form GSSG in a protective mechanism that limits cellular damage especially during oxidative stress. Regulates GSH and GSSG release from astrocytes to maintain glutathione redox equilibrium in the brain (PubMed:16230346, PubMed:8640791). Transports signaling molecules. Appears to selectively recognize cyclic 2'3'-GMP-AMP (cGAMP) produced by mammals but not 3'3'-cGAMP produced by bacteria. Mediates 2'3'-cGAMP export and limits intracellular cGAMP-mediated cGAS-STING signaling and type I interferon synthesis (PubMed:36070769, PubMed:39765229). Exports sphingosine 1-phosphate from mast cells independently of their degranulation (PubMed:17050692). Confers resistance to anticancer drugs by mediating ATP- and GSH-dependent drug export (PubMed:9281595). Similarly to MRP2, transports various steroids, bile acids and bilirubin conjugates (PubMed:8640791, PubMed:9355767)

texts.value: Proofreading amidase that contributes to the maintenance of cell wall composition and integrity (PubMed:28612943, PubMed:35164571, PubMed:40632566). It prevents the mis-incorporation of both L-serine and glycine containing precursors into the peptidoglycan (PG) sacculi (PubMed:28612943, PubMed:35164571, PubMed:40632566). Acts by hydrolyzing UDP-N-acetylmuramoyl-L-serine (UDP-MurNAc-L-Ser) to release L-serine and UDP-N-acetylmuramoyl-glycine (UDP-MurNAc-Gly) to release glycine, thereby preventing the mis-incorporation of these amino acids into the PG and ensuring that only the correct PG precursor, UDP-MurNAc-L-Ala, is incorporated (PubMed:35164571, PubMed:40632566). It can also use UDP-MurNAc-L-Ala, with 10-fold lower activity compared to UDP-MurNAc-L-Ser, and it exhibits weak activity toward UDP-MurNAc-L-Ala-D-Glu (UMAE) and UDP-MurNAc-L-Ser-D-Glu (UMSE) (PubMed:35164571). It does not exhibit PG hydrolytic activity (PubMed:28612943)

The enzyme also shows purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP) activity in vitro (PubMed:31978345). It can catalyze the phosphorolysis of adenosine and inosine nucleosides, yielding D-ribose 1-phosphate and the respective free bases, adenine and hypoxanthine (PubMed:31978345). However, this PNP activity is weak, requires higher protein concentration as compared to the precursor editing activity, and cannot confer growth to a PNP-deficient mutant in vivo, suggesting that it may not be physiologically significant in E.coli (PubMed:40632566). In addition, the enzyme has several other activities in vitro: it can catalyze the phosphorolysis of S-methyl-5'-thioadenosine into adenine and S-methyl-5-thio-alpha-D-ribose 1-phosphate, and it has adenosine deaminase activity (PubMed:31978345). It also shows polyphenol oxidase activity and is able to oxidize syringaldazine and 2,2'-azino-bis(3-ethylbenzthiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) (ABTS) (PubMed:16740638)

All phenotypes of the mutant can be suppressed by a decrease in the intracellular pool of L-serine/glycine (PubMed:28612943). The phenotypes of the mutant are fully complemented by homologs from S.enterica, B.subtilis or G.stearothermophilus (PubMed:40632566)
